$schema.description: The JSON Schema version identifier for this document.

Model.description: An AI model, described by descriptors and model properties.

Coded-data.description: An array of coded data attribute-value items, each using an enumerated code system, a specified 'Other system', or a direct URL to the system and code ID.

examples.Label: Echocardiogram degree of aortic regurgitation status
An ID from an unenumerated coding scheme

System.description: The code system, e.g., SNOMED CT.

Label.description: The text label that describes the code

Value.description: The value of the coded entity

Label.description: The text label that describes the code

Value.description: The value of the coded entity

URL.description: The unique identifier (URL) of the code system and code.

Label.description: The text label that describes the code

Value.description: The value of the coded entity

General-metadata.description: Characteristics of a project, model, or dataset.  Whenever possible, values should link to other ontologies or controlled vocabularies.

Comments.description: Textual comments about the model, dataset, or project.

Contact.description: Physical address or email address of a contact.

Date.description: Dates associated with this resource, such as creation, publication, or update dates.

License.description: License or rights to access this resource

Text.description: Textual name or description of the license.

URL.description: URL pointing to the full text of the license.

References.description: References about the resource, such as a clinical trial identifier or a pointer to a peer-reviewed publication or conference proceedings.

Imaging.description: Imaging modalities, procedures, and other information

Modalities.description: List of imaging modalities used by the model.

items.description: List of imaging modalities; requires value(s) from RadLex:RID10311

Procedures.description: Imaging procedures: each item should include procedure name, RadLex Playbook ID, and/or LOINC code

examples: CT Abdomen and Pelvis W contrast IV

examples.Name: CT Abdomen and Pelvis W contrast IV

Resolution.description: Describes whether the imaging data used original or down-sampled images.

Comments.description: Use this field to specify a file format of type 'Other'.

Acquisition.description: Describes the imaging acquisition equipment and parameters used to obtain the images, such as scanner manufacturer, model, field strength, detector configuration, slice thickness, or reconstruction kernel.

Manufacturer.description: The manufacturer of the imaging equipment used to acquire the images, e.g. GE HealthCare, Siemens Healthineers, Philips, or Canon Medical.

Model.description: The specific model of the imaging equipment used to acquire the images.

Field strength.description: The static magnetic field strength of the MRI scanner used to acquire the images, typically expressed in tesla (T).

Detector configuration.description: The detector configuration of the imaging equipment used to acquire the images, such as the number of detector rows for CT.

Slice thickness.description: The thickness of the reconstructed image slices.

Reconstruction kernel.description: The reconstruction kernel or algorithm applied to raw acquisition data to produce the reconstructed images.

Indexing.description: Indexing codes: Content codes, RadLex, SNOMED, and keywords

SNOMED.description: Array of SNOMED CT concept identifiers (SCTIDs). Integer values are allowed up to 11 digits, which addresses concepts from the International Release. National or local extensions require string values to avoid possibly imprecise interpretation of large integer values. IMPORTANT: The string values are the canonical format; the integer format will be dropped in the next version.

Keywords.description: Array of keywords to index the resource

Integration.description: How the model is integrated into an imaging environment, expressed as interface standards.

Interfaces.description: Interface standards the model supports for input, query and transport.

FHIR.description: HL7 FHIR resources and specifications supported.

IHE profiles.description: IHE Radiology integration profiles to which the model conforms.

Other.description: Interface standards or proprietary interfaces not covered by the enumerated lists.

Result delivery.description: The channels and object types by which model results are returned to the clinical environment.

Conformance statements.description: Pointers to formal conformance documentation. Preferred over prose description of interface support.

System types.description: Categories of clinical system with which the model exchanges data.

Validated systems.description: Named products against which integration has actually been tested. Free text by design: vendor and product names change with acquisitions and cannot be maintained as an enumeration.

Jurisdiction.description: Jurisdiction or regulatory region. Generally ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, except EU (European Union, an economic area) and UK-NI (Northern Ireland, which follows EU MDR under the Windsor Framework rather than UKCA).

Model.description: An AI model, described by general metadata and model properties.

Indexing.description: Indexing information, such as content codes, RadLex + SNOMED codes, and keywords.

Imaging.description: Imaging modalities, procedures, and other imaging-related information relevant to the model.

Model performance.description: An array of tuples that specify the performance of an AI model on a particular set of data.

Factors.description: Declares the axis or axes of subgroup disaggregation examined for this model, e.g. sex, race/ethnicity, age group, or site. Individual disaggregated results are recorded via each performance result's Subgroup.

Datasets.description: Datasets associated with the model's development, disaggregated by role (e.g. training, validation, test).

Dataset.description: Pointer to or description of the dataset.

URL.description: Pointer to the dataset, e.g. a dataset card conforming to the ATLAS dataset schema (preferred)

Role.description: The dataset's role in the model's development.

Model-performance.description: An array of tuples that specify the performance of an AI model on a particular set of data.

Evaluation dataset.description: Data on which the model has been evaluated. One of more results (index text, value, confidence interval) for each dataset

Description.description: Textual description of the evaluation dataset

Results.description: The metric results for this evaluation.

Provenance.description: Indicates whether this performance record is claimed (self-reported by the developer, e.g. from internal or external testing) or observed (derived from real-world, deployed use, e.g. registry-reported concordance).

Metric justification.description: Explains why the metric(s) reported are appropriate measures of performance for this specific model and its intended use.

Test type.description: The relationship between the data used to evaluate an AI model and the data used to develop it, together with the point in the model's lifecycle at which the evaluation was performed.

Testing agent.description: Person or organization that conducted external testing

Model-performance-results.description: Array of tuples: (index test, metric, value), each either a scalar-metric result (a numeric value with an optional confidence interval) or a non-scalar-metric result (a string or URL value, e.g. a markdown table or a link to a matrix or graph).

items.description: Tuple of index test, metric, value.

Index test.description: Describes what is being measured. For example, not simply large vessel occlusion (LVO), but M2/M3 LVO.

Scalar metric.description: The scalar metric used to measure performance.

Value.description: The observed value of the metric.

Level.description: Confidence level, expressed as a decimal value

Subgroup.description: Identifies the specific subgroup for which this result was computed, when this result is disaggregated by one of the model's declared Factors.

Index test.description: Describes what is being measured. For example, not simply large vessel occlusion (LVO), but M2/M3 LVO.

Subgroup.description: Identifies the specific subgroup for which this result was computed, when this result is disaggregated by one of the model's declared Factors.

Index test.description: Describes what is being measured. For example, not simply large vessel occlusion (LVO), but M2/M3 LVO.

Nonscalar metric.description: The non-scalar (graphical or matrix) metric used to measure performance.

Value.description: The non-scalar metric's value, expressed either as a string (e.g. a markdown table) or as a URL pointing to an external matrix or graph resource.

Subgroup.description: Identifies the specific subgroup for which this result was computed, when this result is disaggregated by one of the model's declared Factors.

Architecture.description: Textual description of underlying model technology, e.g., "Convolutional Neural Network".

Model class.description: The general architectural or algorithmic category of the model, as a coarse, queryable category distinct from the free-text Architecture description.

Foundation model.description: The pretrained foundation model this model is built upon, fine-tuned from, or otherwise directly incorporates, if any.

Provider.description: Organization that developed or distributes the foundation model.

Third-party components.description: Third-party or pre-trained components incorporated into the model, other than a foundation model captured separately, such as pretrained encoders or vendor SDKs material to the model's behavior.

Provider.description: Organization or project that developed or distributes the component.

Availability.description: Defines where and/or how the model is available; can include a URL.

Clinical benefit.description: Clinical benefits, such as diagnosis, risk assessment, or treatment selection.

Clinical workflow phase.description: Clinical workflow phase (e.g., patient pre-registration, digitization of forms or clinical  scales, patients' triage, telehealth & virtual rounds, clinical decision support systems, workflow optimization, evidence-based methods to optimize medical interventions, feedback from users).

Degree of automation.description: Degree of automation compared to the current standard of care, including whether the device supports or automates decision making.

Indications for use.description: The indications for use describe: (1) the disease or condition that the AI system will diagnose, treat, prevent, cure, or mitigate; (2) the intended patient population; and (3) the intended use environment (e.g., ICU, step-down unit, home).

Input.description: Describes the type(s) of information used as input into the model; for example, abdomen/pelvis CT images and laboratory data.

Coded data.description: Coded data elements using RadLex, RadElement, SNOMED CT, LOINC, etc.

Instructions.description: Directions and recommendations for optimal use of the model.

Limitations.description: Describes concerns specific to the use of the AI model. Includes: (1) Known biases or failure modes; (2) Known gaps in the data characterization, such as patient populations that are not well represented in development (e.g., training) or testing datasets, and therefore, may be at risk of bias; (3) Limitations in the model development or performance evaluation; and (4) Known circumstances where the device input will not align with the data used in development and validation.

Output.description: Describes the type of output produced by the model, such as classification (diagnosis) results or image segmentation.

Type.description: The general category of the value produced by the model as output.

Coded data.description: Coded data elements using RadLex, RadElement, SNOMED CT, LOINC, etc.

Regulatory information.description: Information used to support or document regulatory review, covering one or more jurisdiction-specific authorization pathways (e.g. FDA, CE marking under EU MDR, UKCA).

Authorizations.description: One record per jurisdiction/pathway. Absence of a record does not imply absence of authorization; use Status "Not submitted" to state this explicitly. A model may hold more than one record, e.g. an original 510(k) plus supplements, or authorizations in multiple jurisdictions.

Jurisdiction.description: Jurisdiction or regulatory region in which this authorization was granted or sought.

Authority.description: Regulatory authority or conformity-assessment body responsible for the authorization.

Authority identifier.description: Notified Body or Approved Body number, where applicable.

Status.description: Status of this authorization. "Not submitted" and "Research use only" are positive assertions and should be used in preference to omitting the record. "Not available" mirrors the ONC convention at 45 CFR 170.315(b)(11)(v)(A)(2).

Identifier.description: Submission or certificate number. FDA identifiers follow a fixed format (see examples); CE and UKCA certificate numbers are assigned in Notified/Approved Body house formats and vary.

Risk class.description: Jurisdiction-specific risk classification; not comparable across jurisdictions and should be interpreted only together with Jurisdiction.

Predicate device.description: 510(k) only. Predicate device identifier or name.

UDI-DI.description: Unique Device Identifier - Device Identifier, the model/version-level identifier assigned under a UDI system such as EUDAMED or the FDA GUDID.

Basic UDI-DI.description: Basic Unique Device Identifier - Device Identifier, the primary identifier of a device model grouping, used in EUDAMED and other UDI systems independent of packaging/version-level UDI-DIs.

Registry URL.description: Deep link to the public registry entry, where one exists.

EU AI Act.description: Co-classification under Regulation (EU) 2024/1689. Independent of CE marking under MDR: a device may hold both.

Technical documentation.description: Status of the Annex IV technical documentation.

Change control.description: Predetermined change control, e.g. an FDA or MHRA Predetermined Change Control Plan (PCCP), or the technical solutions for continuous compliance described at EU AI Act Annex IV point 2(f). A plan may cover more than one jurisdiction.

PCCP in place.description: Indicates whether a predetermined change control plan is in place for this model.

Description.description: Description of the predetermined change control plan, such as the anticipated changes and the methods used to develop and validate them.

Jurisdictions.description: Jurisdictions in which this change control plan has been reviewed or accepted.

Harmonized standards applied.description: Lists the harmonized standards, common specifications, or other technical standards applied in developing and evaluating the model, or the solutions adopted to meet the applicable requirements in their absence.

Reproducibility.description: Describes the AI model's reproducibility associated with the provided outputs.

Sustainability.description: Describes parameters associated with use of the AI model related to energy consumption, running time, and other factors.

Computational resources.description: Describes the computational resources (e.g., processor type and count, memory, accelerators) used to develop, train, test, and validate the model, as distinct from the resources needed to apply it.

Cybersecurity measures.description: Describes cybersecurity measures put in place for the AI model, such as access controls, vulnerability management, or secure update mechanisms.

Distribution form.description: The form(s) in which the model is placed on the market or put into service.

User interface.description: A basic description of the user interface provided to the deployer for interacting with the model's outputs.

Acceptance test procedure.description: A recommended procedure by which a receiving site can verify the model's performance on local data before deployment.

Operating range.description: A declared expected performance range or minimum performance floor, used to detect when the model's real-world performance has fallen outside acceptable bounds.

Suspend-use conditions.description: Conditions, such as a specific performance decline or an operational change, under which use of the model should be suspended.

Maintenance.description: Describes how the model's real-world performance and fairness are monitored, and the process by which the model is updated in response.

Monitoring program.description: Name of the real-world performance monitoring program or registry the model is enrolled in, if any, e.g. the ACR Assess-AI registry.

Validity monitoring.description: Describes how the model's real-world performance is monitored for validity (e.g. drift, degradation) after deployment.

Fairness monitoring.description: Describes how the model's real-world performance is monitored for fairness across subgroups after deployment.

Update process.description: Describes the process by which the model is updated in response to monitoring findings, such as retraining triggers or a predetermined change control plan.

Bias mitigation approach.description: Describes the approach taken during model development to identify, manage, reduce, or eliminate bias, and to help ensure the model's output is fair across relevant subgroups.

Clinical risk level.description: A declared level of clinical risk associated with use of the model, such as a risk classification scheme used by the developer or a relevant regulatory framework.

Other.description: Use(s) other than the enumerated values, specified as text.

Other user.description: User(s) other than the enumerated values, specified as text. Should specify intended, etc.

Nonscalar-metric.description: Enumerated list of graphical and matrix metrics

Contact name.description: Name or role of organizational contact

examples: 820 Jorie Blvd, Oak Brook, IL 60523-2251, USA

Outcome-counts.description: List of outcome counts, which populate the cells and marginal totals of a binary confusion matrix

ORCID.description: Unique ORCID (Open Researcher and Contributor ID) identifier

Reference.description: A reference about the resource, such as a clinical trial identifier or a pointer to a peer-reviewed publication or conference proceedings

examples: The RSNA Abdominal Traumatic Injury CT (RATIC) Dataset

Source.description: Name of journal, book, or other source; or full citation (see example)

Clinical trial.description: A clinical trial identifier or URL, such as issued by ClinicalTrials.gov

Scalar-metric.description: Enumerated list of scalar metrics. The list includes sensitivity, specificity, precision, and recall as frequently-used terms; they all are alternate terms (e.g., for true positive rate).
enum: area under the alternative free-response operating characteristic curve
area under the predictive receiver operating characteristic curve
area under the receiver operating characteristic curve
AUC of each class vs. each of the other k-1 classes
AUC of each class vs. the rest combined
expected calibration error with kernel density estimate
fraction of cases with user adjustment
integrated time-dependent area under the ROC curve
number of positive cases needed to benefit
partial area under the receiver operating characteristic curve
time-dependent area under the receiver operating characteristic curve

Subgroup.description: Identifies a specific subgroup, for use when a performance result is disaggregated by one of the model's declared Factors.

Variable.description: The factor or axis of disaggregation.

Value.description: The specific subgroup value within that variable.
